걷다.forms: 걸어요 · 걸었어요 · 걸을 거예요 · 걸으세요 (ㄷ irregular)
걷다.x: I walk in the park every day.
걷다.t: ㄷ irregular: 걷다 → 걸어요. Don't confuse with regular 걸다 'to hang', which also gives 걸어요.

맛있다.x: This kimchi stew is really delicious.
맛있다.e: 맛 (taste) + 있다 (have) = 'has taste'. Sounds like 마싣따.
맛있다.t: Words ending in 있다/없다 take -는 before a noun: 맛있는 음식 (not 맛있은).

아직.forms: 아직 + negative: 아직 안 왔어요 · 아직 + positive: 아직 자요 (still)
아직.e: 아직 안 했어요 = I haven't done it yet.
아직.t: With a negative it means 'not yet'; with a positive it means 'still'.

지하철역.ex: 우리 집에서 지하철역까지 걸어서 오 분 걸려요.
지하철역.x: It's a five-minute walk from my house to the subway station.
지하철역.t: Pronounced [지하철력]: an ㄴ sound is added before 역 and then becomes ㄹ after ㄹ.

문법.x: Korean grammar was a little difficult at first.

삼겹살.x: Yesterday I grilled pork belly with my friends.
삼겹살.e: 삼 'three' + 겹 'layer' + 살 'flesh': three layers of fat and meat.

첫째.ex: 우리 집 첫째는 올해 대학생이 됐어요.
첫째.x: The eldest in our family became a college student this year.
첫째.e: From 첫 'first' plus -째 'order'; the ordinal for 하나.
첫째.t: Ordinals add -째 to native numbers, but 'first' is irregular: 첫째, not 한째.

시청자.ex: 이 드라마는 많은 시청자들에게 사랑을 받았어요.
시청자.x: This drama was loved by many viewers.
시청자.e: -자 = person who does it: 시청자, 참가자, 운전자.

교육하다.m: to educate, to teach, to train
교육하다.ex: 회사에서 신입 사원을 한 달 동안 교육해요.
교육하다.x: The company trains new employees for a month.
교육하다.t: Pronounced [교유카다]: ㄱ plus ㅎ merges into an aspirated ㅋ.

완벽하다.x: His Korean pronunciation is almost perfect.
완벽하다.e: Literally 'a complete jade disc', from a Chinese story about returning a jade disc unbroken.

부담스럽다.m: to be burdensome, to feel pressured, to feel like too much
부담스럽다.x: An expensive gift feels like a bit much.
부담스럽다.e: 부담 'burden' plus -스럽다 'feeling like': it feels like a burden.
부담스럽다.t: Koreans also use it for too much attention or kindness, like a stare or a pushy friend.

의사소통.ex: 외국인 친구와 의사소통이 잘 돼서 좋아요.
의사소통.x: I'm happy that I can communicate well with my foreign friend.
의사소통.t: Here 의사 means 'intention', not 의사 'doctor'; they're different words that sound the same.

민속놀이.x: On Lunar New Year, we play traditional folk games with the family.
민속놀이.e: Sino 민속 'folk custom' plus native 놀이 'game, play'.
민속놀이.t: Pronounced [민송노리] — the ㄱ becomes ㅇ before ㄴ (nasalization).

상상력.x: Children have richer imaginations than adults.
상상력.e: -력 = power or ability: 상상력, 기술력, 노력.
상상력.t: Pronounced [상상녁] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

시행.ex: 새 제도의 시행으로 많은 것이 바뀌었어요.
시행.x: Many things changed with the implementation of the new system.

원망.ex: 일이 잘못되어도 저는 아무도 원망하지 않아요.
원망.x: Even if things go wrong, I don't blame anyone.
원망.e: Literally 'resentful longing' — wishing things had been otherwise.
원망.t: Often used toward people close to you or fate: 하늘을 원망하다 'to curse the heavens'.

즉흥적.ex: 우리는 주말에 즉흥적으로 바다에 가기로 했어요.
즉흥적.x: We spontaneously decided to go to the beach on the weekend.
즉흥적.e: Literally 'immediate mood' — acting on the feeling of the moment.
즉흥적.t: Pronounced [즈킁적]; more neutral than 충동적 and often positive, like a spontaneous trip.

순식간에.m: in an instant, in the blink of an eye
순식간에.x: The cake was all gone in the blink of an eye.
순식간에.e: Literally 'in the space of a blink and a breath'.
순식간에.t: Pronounced [순식까네] — the ㄱ after ㄱ becomes tense.
rel: in the blink of an eye

손쉽다.ex: 요즘은 스마트폰으로 손쉽게 은행 일을 볼 수 있어요.
손쉽다.x: These days you can easily do your banking on a smartphone.
손쉽다.e: Built from 손 'hand' + 쉽다 'easy' — easy enough to do by hand.
손쉽다.t: Mostly used as the adverb 손쉽게 (easily, with little effort).

침입.x: A burglar broke into a store in our neighborhood last night.
침입.t: 침략 is a nation's aggression; 침입 is any forced entry, from burglars to viruses.

갯벌.x: On the weekend, I dug for clams on the mudflat with the kids.
갯벌.e: From 개 'tidal inlet' + 벌 'open flat land'; the ㅅ links the two parts.
갯벌.t: Korea's west coast mudflats are famous; 갯벌 체험 'mudflat experience' is a popular family outing.

내성.ex: 항생제를 자주 먹으면 내성이 생길 수 있어요.
내성.x: If you take antibiotics often, you can build up resistance.
내성.e: Literally 'enduring nature' — the body or germ gets used to it.
내성.t: Homonym warning: 내성적 (內省的) means introverted, a completely different word.

돌입하다.m: to rush into, to enter (a phase such as a strike or campaign)
돌입하다.x: The labor union went on a general strike starting this morning.
돌입하다.e: Literally 'burst in' — plunging suddenly into a new phase.

일축하다.m: to dismiss, to reject out of hand, to brush off
일축하다.x: The minister dismissed rumors of his resignation.
일축하다.e: Literally 'one kick', kicking something away with a single move.
일축하다.t: A news staple for flat denials: 의혹을 일축하다 = to dismiss allegations.

전락하다.m: to fall (into a worse state), to degenerate, to be reduced to
전락하다.ex: 한때 인기 있던 관광지가 이제는 쓰레기장으로 전락했어요.
전락하다.x: A once-popular tourist spot has now been reduced to a dump.
전락하다.t: Pronounced [절라카다]. Pattern: N(으)로 전락하다 'to be reduced to N.'

탈북자.ex: 탈북자들이 한국 사회에 적응하는 것은 쉽지 않아요.
탈북자.x: It isn't easy for North Korean defectors to adapt to South Korean society.
탈북자.e: Literally 'person who escaped the North'. -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.
탈북자.t: Pronounced [탈북짜]; many prefer the softer term 북한이탈주민 in official contexts.

출생률.ex: 한국의 출생률은 세계에서 가장 낮은 수준이에요.
출생률.x: Korea's birth rate is among the lowest in the world.
출생률.t: Pronounced [출쌩뉼]; -률 follows consonants, -율 follows vowels or ㄴ.

교통난.x: Traffic congestion is really serious during rush hour.
교통난.e: -난 = shortage or trouble: 교통난, 주차난, 취업난.

지성인.ex: 지성인이라면 사회 문제에 관심을 가져야 합니다.
지성인.x: An intellectual should take an interest in social issues.

도덕률.ex: 칸트는 마음속의 도덕률을 늘 경이롭게 여겼어요.
도덕률.x: Kant always regarded the moral law within him with wonder.
도덕률.t: Pronounced [도덩뉼]; this ending is spelled -율 after a vowel or ㄴ, as in 규율 and 비율.

양자역학.ex: 양자역학은 아주 작은 입자의 움직임을 설명합니다.
양자역학.x: Quantum mechanics explains the behavior of very small particles.
양자역학.t: Pronounced [양자여칵]; 역학 shows up in many physics field names.

가동률.x: Orders dropped, so the factory's operating rate fell to 70 percent.
가동률.e: Literally 'running rate'; 가동 means a machine or plant is running.
가동률.t: Pronounced [가동뉼]; the suffix 'rate' is written 률 after a consonant, but 율 after a vowel or ㄴ.

조형예술.ex: 회화와 조각, 건축은 모두 대표적인 조형예술입니다.
조형예술.x: Painting, sculpture and architecture are all typical examples of the visual arts.

화랑.x: On the weekend I saw an exhibition at a gallery in Insa-dong.
화랑.t: Not to be confused with 화랑 (花郞), the elite youth corps of ancient Silla.

암행어사.ex: 암행어사는 몰래 지방을 다니며 수령들을 감시했어요.
암행어사.x: Secret royal inspectors traveled the provinces in disguise, watching the magistrates.
암행어사.e: Literally 'royal official who travels in secret'.
암행어사.t: The famous cry 암행어사 출두요! means the inspector is revealing himself, as in The Tale of Chunhyang.

사장되다.m: to lie unused, to be shelved, to go to waste
사장되다.x: A good idea was shelved due to a lack of budget.
사장되다.e: Literally 'stored dead': kept away where it is never used.
사장되다.t: Homonym warning: 사장 (社長) is 'company president.' 사장되다 has nothing to do with bosses.

처량하다.ex: 비를 맞고 서 있는 모습이 처량해 보였어요.
처량하다.x: Standing there in the rain, he looked forlorn.

전도유망.ex: 그녀는 학계에서 주목받는 전도유망한 젊은 과학자입니다.
전도유망.x: She is a promising young scientist drawing attention in academia.
전도유망.t: Usually used as an adjective: 전도유망한 + person, e.g. 전도유망한 선수.

포복절도.m: laughing so hard one doubles over
포복절도.ex: 그 코미디 영화는 관객들을 포복절도하게 만들었어요.
포복절도.x: That comedy had the audience doubled over with laughter.
포복절도.e: Literally 'clutching one's belly and falling over.'
포복절도.t: Pronounced [포복쩔또]; don't confuse 포복 'clutching the belly' here with 포복 'crawling.'
